input.question: How can airbnb inflate rental and housing prices; shouldn't competition drive down prices?
input.ground_truth: AirBnB drives down ***short term rental*** prices. AKA "hotel" prices. It does this at the expense of decreasing the housing supply and ***driving up*** prices for long-term accommodations like homes and condos. In a simple supply and demand equation, it increases the supply of SHORT TERM accommodation (like hotel rooms) - reducing their cost- and decreases the supply of long-term accommodations (like houses) - increasing their cost.

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

I am a woman.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How can airbnb inflate rental and housing prices; shouldn't competition drive down prices?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you and your friends all want to sell lemonade on the same street. Normally, if lots of people are selling lemonade, you’d all have to make your lemonade cheaper to get people to buy from you, right? That’s how competition works—when lots of people are selling the same thing, they try to make it cheaper to get more customers.

But now, let’s say there’s a big lemonade machine that only some of you can use, and it makes making lemonade a lot easier and faster. Those friends with the machine can make more lemonade and charge a little more because it’s so easy for them. Also, if most people only know about the big machine people, they might not look for the others who are selling lemonade the old way.

Now, think of Airbnb like that big lemonade machine. It makes it super easy for people to rent out their homes, and lots of people look on Airbnb to find a place to stay. But when so many people use Airbnb, some landlords see that they can make more money by renting to Airbnb instead of having someone live there for a long time. Because of this, there are fewer regular homes for people to live in, so the prices for regular apartments can go up.

Also, if everyone wants to stay in a cool place they see on Airbnb, they might be willing to pay more, so the prices go up even more. Even though there are lots of listings (like lots of lemonade stands), the fact that it’s so popular and that some places are harder to find (like regular apartments to rent) can make prices go up instead of down.

So, even with lots of competition on Airbnb, the whole situation can make housing prices go up in the neighborhood because it changes how people rent and buy homes.
